subject: gravity.arcs.care, all five pages (overview + four seats), read as Kyle Libra from his 24 Substack posts
headline: His engine makes ideas cheap.
His footnote says the filter is the hard part.
lede: Source: all 24 posts on kylelibra.substack.com (2025-08-22 to 2026-09-21), read in full, plus his profile export. The gauntlet read the five Gravity pages as six versions of him, then a seventh pass rejected over-flags and ranked the rest.

sections.title: The mirror
sections.tagline: Not better physics. His own sentence.

rows.text: He calls his own gravity sim "a sort of web based fidget spinner" that may become the studio brand. One-upping it is the most expensive move on the board, and cosmic words for a dated log trip his "grandiose marketing language" flag.
Tuning the filter is "by far the most difficult" part of the Idea Engine. ARCS keeps the record of which filter calls held up.
"significance is in the eye of the beholder and AI is not particularly good at assessing it", and he floated "a simple Eval framework".

rows.signal: Credit his toy in one line
rows.text: "You called your gravity sim a web-based fidget spinner. Mine is less fun: a dated list of which calls landed."

tabs.label: Thesis
tabs.name: Kyle Libra, in his own words
tabs.headline: Distribution over issuance; activity over size; most ideas die.
tabs.lede: Advisor at Gravity Labs since Oct 2026 (CEO May to Oct 2026, partner before). Paxos Head of Brokerage Product 2019 to 2025: BUSD, PYUSD, USDG. Web developer 2006 to 2010.

rows.text: Issuers end up with BlackRock margins, not Visa margins; "whoever owns distribution is going to be able to force adoption" (2025-09-16).
Transaction count and volume over market cap; the price of Bitcoin is the wrong gauge of adoption (2026-02-09, 2025-09-25).
Regulated, fully backed dollar stables first; Robinhood and Coinbase race JPMorgan; slower than tech usually moves because of regulation, which he sees as healthy (2025-11-26).
About 19 of 20 memos shelved; 1 of 29 stage-3 memos funded; "Getting projects to no... is just as valuable as yes" (2026-01-23, 2026-03-30).
Idea Engine: 6x faster to a good memo, $100 of tokens saves $300k of analyst time; AI is "particularly bad at inventing the future" (2026-09-21).

head: Test
His words (2026-08-07)
rows: Can this person identify real pain points?
How much effort was required to ship this?
Is the approach so wrong it would stunt adoption?
Why couldn't they get 10 people on the phone the next day?
Scope vs vision mismatch; grandiose language; blue or purple on black; superfluous copy
Frame this as one of many; show a long list of things you've built

blocks.text: Plain, self-deprecating, footnote-heavy. Calls evals "just a test framework", calls his own script an agent with a wink, cringes at posting on LinkedIn. Publishes results he did not like: "I'm posting this because I said I would." 18 side projects in a year; Mogg, a free daily YES/NO prediction game, from the studio (2026-06-24).
Distribution over issuance is a practitioner's call, and activity over size is the right lens. The studio thesis is honest about survivorship bias.

He has a volume engine and a hand-tuned filter, and no record of which of his judgments came true. His own footnotes name it. That is the gap ARCS fills, and his sentence, not a metaphor, is the way in.

findings_lede: Facets: his own checklist, the Paxos practitioner, the studio operator, the proposed frame, the hype skeptic, the 60-second advisor. Cyan rows are fixed or kept out in PR 2138; #6 needs calls only Zach can make (not now, Zach 2026-11-11).
